risks.title: Persistent Elevated Inflation and Interest Rate Uncertainty
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above central bank targets, leading to continued uncertainty about the path of monetary policy. This persistence complicates efforts to return to price stability without harming economic growth.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings, Federal Reserve statements on future rate hikes, and market pricing of interest rate futures.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement / SEP / minutes), September 2026
Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes), September 2026
Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.summary: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, continue to disrupt global supply chains, leading to elevated energy and commodity prices and contributing to inflationary pressures.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, energy price movements (oil and gas), and reports of new supply chain bottlenecks.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement / SEP / minutes), September 2026
Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes), September 2026
Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Economic Dependence
risks.summary: The rapid buildout of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a significant driver of investment and growth, but the economy's increasing reliance on this narrow set of drivers poses a risk if the AI investment thesis falters.
risks.watch_for: Corporate capital expenditure plans for AI, profitability of AI-related firms, and any signs of a slowdown in AI investment.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes), September 2026
Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

risks.title: Slowing Global Growth Amidst Divergent Economic Paths
risks.summary: Global economic growth is projected to slow in 2026, with divergent performance across regions. Emerging markets and developing economies are particularly vulnerable to the ongoing energy shock and geopolitical uncertainties.
risks.watch_for: IMF and World Bank global growth forecasts, regional economic performance indicators, and trade data.

risks.title: Fiscal Policy Constraints and Rising Debt Levels
risks.summary: Governments face increasing pressure to finance demands, including defense spending and AI investments, while also managing rising national debt. This limits fiscal space for stimulus and increases vulnerability to financial crises.
risks.watch_for: Government budget deficits and debt-to-GDP ratios, announcements of new fiscal stimulus or austerity measures, and sovereign debt ratings.
sources: Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

risks.title: Labor Market Dynamics and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While the labor market shows resilience with stable unemployment, concerns about affordability persist for consumers, particularly low- and middle-income households. The impact of AI on jobs also remains a focus.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate, wage growth, consumer sentiment surveys, and data on AI adoption in the workforce.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement / SEP / minutes), September 2026
Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes), September 2026
Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

risks.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Tariffs
risks.summary: Ongoing trade tensions and the potential for new tariffs create uncertainty, impacting global trade flows, supply chains, and potentially leading to further economic fragmentation.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs or trade disputes, changes in trade volumes, and statements from trade organizations.
sources: Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), September 2026

consensus_note: There is a strong consensus across institutions regarding the persistent nature of inflation and the ongoing risks posed by geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions. While AI investment is seen as a growth driver, its concentration as a key economic engine is flagged as a potential vulnerability. Divergent global growth paths and fiscal policy constraints are also widely recognized concerns.
